fatal_errors: The proposed testing regime of tensile or flexural loading at approximately 1200 °C does not reconstruct the reported quasi-static compression, indentation from room temperature to 500 °C, or room-temperature scratch testing.
The hypothesis attributes enhanced plasticity to dynamic recrystallization and grain-boundary sliding, neither of which was demonstrated or invoked by the target evidence.

It reverses the observed strength comparison by predicting lower HEA yield strength and higher tungsten yield strength; the measured HEA yield strength remained substantially above tungsten through 500 °C.
The proposed HEA-versus-tungsten comparison does not isolate lattice distortion because composition, phase constitution, segregation, grain structure, and processing route all differ simultaneously.
It assumes a homogeneous high-entropy microstructure, whereas the alloy was a solidification-segregated, two-BCC-phase dendritic material.
Claims about sustained plasma-facing service are unsupported because irradiation and operating fusion-environment performance were not tested.
explanation: The response addresses the broad alloy-versus-tungsten plasticity and toughness question and supplies a nominally falsifiable comparison, but it does not agree with the relevant material state, conditions, mechanism, or strength outcome. The supported interpretation combines solid-solution/lattice-distortion strengthening with possible Ti/V/Zr-mediated changes in dislocation behavior, cohesion, localized plasticity, and crack impedance; these assignments were themselves not causally isolated. The generated account instead makes unsubstantiated claims that lattice distortion reduces pinning and causes grain-boundary sliding and dynamic recrystallization. It also extrapolates from the tested room-temperature-to-500 °C regime to at least 1000–1200 °C sustained service. Its experiment could test whether the proposed phenomena occur at 1200 °C, but cannot identify lattice distortion as the cause without microstructurally matched controls. No supporting prior evidence is cited.
